fixture_name: Six HAWK pedestrian crossings — US final design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Nighttime conspicuity of a HAWK display controlling an arterial crossing is a substantive final-design-stage safety issue with direct crash potential for crossing pedestrians.
justifications.evidence_grounding: The pivotal claim (driver confusion from competing background elements at night at this site) is backed by a verbatim quote from EV-US-001 tied to the recorded FHWA case-study issue.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a categorical safety_concern with no asserted MUTCD non-compliance, consistent with FHWA RSA framework semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Reflective border/backplate treatment is a specific, actionable, and viable countermeasure at final design, targeted at the identified conspicuity problem.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians—the exposed VRUs at the crossing—are explicitly identified and linked to the driver-detection failure mode.

justifications.substance: Pedestrian clearance interval adequacy for slower walkers at the corridor's highest pedestrian/bicycle collision frequency HAWK sites is a recognized, substantive final-design-stage safety issue.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Verbatim quoted case-study text (EV-US-016) directly supports the pivotal claim that the clearance interval may be short particularly for elderly pedestrians at these recorded sites.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Properly framed as a safety_concern seeking verification of design assumptions, cleanly separated from any MUTCD compliance assertion about required clearance times.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: reprogramme clearance intervals at all six named HAWK crossings using a reduced assumed walking speed, a standard and viable final-design remedy.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and elderly pedestrians are the explicit focus of the finding, with VRU exposure at conflict-release transitions squarely addressed.
